definition: The in-crowd algorithm is a numerical method for solving basis pursuit denoising quickly; faster than any other algorithm for large, sparse problems.
details: This algorithm is an active set method, which minimizes iteratively sub-problems of the global basis pursuit denoising: min x 1 2 ‖ y − A x ‖ 2 2 + λ ‖ x ‖ 1 . {\displaystyle \min _{x}{\frac {1}{2}}\|y-Ax\|_{2}^{2}+\lambda \|x\|_{1}.} where y {\displaystyle y} is the observed signal, x {\displaystyle x} is the sparse signal to be recovered, A x {\displaystyle Ax} is the expected signal under x {\displaystyle x} , and λ {\displaystyle \lambda } is the regularization parameter trading off signal fidelity and simplicity. The simplicity is here measured using the sparsity of the solution x {\displaystyle x} , measure through its ℓ 1 {\displaystyle \ell _{1}} -norm. The active set strategies are very efficient in this context as only few coefficient are expected to be non-zero. Thus, if they can be identified, solving the problem restricted to these coefficients yield the solution. Here, the features are greedily selected based on the absolute value of their gradient at the current estimate. Other active-set methods for the basis pursuit denoising includes BLITZ, where the selection of the active set is performed using the duality gap of the problem, and The Feature Sign Search, where the features are included based on the estimate of their sign.

explainer.lead: The in-crowd algorithm is a numerical method for solving basis pursuit denoising quickly, reported faster than other algorithms for large, sparse problems. It matters because sparse recovery on large problems is otherwise slow.

tiers.eli5: It's a fast way to find the few important pieces that explain a big messy signal, skipping the unimportant parts.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it as an active-set method that repeatedly solves smaller sub-problems of the global objective. A pitfall is that performance depends on the sparsity structure of the problem.
tiers.paperLevel: It is an active-set method minimizing, iteratively, sub-problems of basis pursuit denoising: min over x of one half times the squared L2 norm of y minus A x, plus lambda times the L1 norm of x, where y is the observed signal, x the sparse signal, A x the expected signal and lambda the regularization parameter. Limits concern the sparsity regime it is designed for.

explainer.example: Given a large observation y and a wide matrix A, the algorithm solves the regularized sparse recovery by working on active subsets of variables rather than all of them at once.
